title: Platform On‑Call Quick Reference: Shell Helpers & Operator Scripts
author: Leah Morgan
content:
Overview
========

Shortcuts and vetted shell helpers that platform operators use during on‑call shifts for common remediation, triage, and lightweight automation tasks. This page is a compact, copy‑paste friendly quick reference intended for experienced platform operators; it complements longer runbooks and automation libraries.

Purpose
-------
- Reduce cognitive load during incidents by consolidating high‑value, low‑risk shell helpers.
- Provide safe defaults, guardrails, and a short testing checklist for each helper.
- Make it easy to discover approved one‑liners and small scripts that are safe to run from the operator jump host.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Audience: Platform operators and SREs who are already familiar with Redwood runtime processes.
- Scope: Non‑destructive helpers for: traffic shaping, tenant drain, KV/prefix cache inspection and warmup, model swap in a compatible variant, telemetry checks, and token cost triage.
- Not covered: full cluster automation (use CI/CD pipelines) and high-risk destructive commands (privileged DB migrations, mass evictions).

Ownership and conventions
------------------------
- Owner: eng-platform oncall cookbook team (primary contact: @leah.morgan).
- Naming: scripts follow pattern: rw-<area>-<action>.sh and live in /opt/platform-ops/bin on jump hosts.
- Logging: every helper writes a compact audit line to /var/log/platform-operator-actions.log using the add_audit helper below.

Prerequisites
-------------
- SSH to operator jump host (platform-jump.redwood.internal) with operator role.
- Kube context set to the region namespace: e.g., rw-prod-us-east.
- Environment helpers installed: rwctl, telemetry-proxy, jq, yq, curl.

Common helpers (catalog)
------------------------
The table below lists the canonical helpers and a short description. Path: /opt/platform-ops/bin (jump hosts) and mirrored in repository infra/platform-ops/scripts.

| Script | Purpose | Safety notes | Example |
|--------|---------|--------------|---------|
| rw-add-audit.sh | Append an operator action to the centralized audit log | Idempotent, non-blocking | sudo rw-add-audit.sh "eviction:tenant-1234:soft-drain" |
| rw-drain-tenant.sh | Initiate soft drain (graceful) for a tenant slice | Dry-run flag; does not evict in dry-run | sudo rw-drain-tenant.sh --tenant tenant-1234 --dry-run |
| rw-prefetch-model.sh | Warm model KV/prefix cache for a tenant workload | Rate limited to avoid token storm | sudo rw-prefetch-model.sh --model redwood-ggml-7b --prefix "user:tenant-1234" --tokens 1000 |
| rw-telemetry-check.sh | Health and histogram snapshot of telemetry pipeline for a region | Read-only; quick checks only | sudo rw-telemetry-check.sh --region us-east |
| rw-swap-model-variant.sh | Swap to a compatible fallback model (canary then instant) | Built-in canary traffic split; requires approval label | sudo rw-swap-model-variant.sh --service inference-prod --from redwood-7b-q8 --to redwood-7b-q4-canary --canary 5 |
| rw-token-bucket-audit.sh | Produce a token consumption summary for a tenant over last 60m | Read-only; may be heavy on telemetry-proxy | sudo rw-token-bucket-audit.sh --tenant tenant-1234 --minutes 60 |

Approved one‑liners and operator recipes
--------------------------------------
Copy‑paste friendly snippets. Always run with --dry-run first if available.

1) Quick cache warmup for low‑impact prefix (safe pattern)

```bash
# dry-run: estimate tokens that will be requested
sudo /opt/platform-ops/bin/rw-prefetch-model.sh --model redwood-ggml-7b --prefix "system:prompt-warmup" --tokens 100 --dry-run

# execute with rate limit and operator tag
sudo /opt/platform-ops/bin/rw-prefetch-model.sh --model redwood-ggml-7b --prefix "system:prompt-warmup" --tokens 100 --rate 10/s --operator "$USER"
```

2) Soft drain + check in 10 minutes (tenant evacuation pattern)

```bash
# mark tenant as draining (non-blocking)
sudo /opt/platform-ops/bin/rw-drain-tenant.sh --tenant tenant-1234 --reason "investigating latency spike" --dry-run

# verify active requests drop below threshold (< 5 concurrent)
sudo rwctl tenant-requests --tenant tenant-1234 --region us-east | awk '{print $2}' | grep -E '^[0-9]+$'

# after verifying, run without dry-run
sudo /opt/platform-ops/bin/rw-drain-tenant.sh --tenant tenant-1234 --reason "investigating latency spike"
```

3) Canary model swap (5% traffic) and automated rollback schedule

```bash
# create canary and schedule automatic rollback after 20m unless promoted
sudo /opt/platform-ops/bin/rw-swap-model-variant.sh --service inference-prod --from redwood-7b-q8 --to redwood-7b-q4-canary --canary 5 --auto-rollback 20m --operator "$USER"

# monitor canary metrics (latency, token-cost-per-response, quality-regressions)
watch -n 10 \ 
  "curl -s 'http://telemetry-proxy.internal/metrics?service=inference-prod&variant=redwood-7b-q4-canary' | jq '.metrics | {latency_p95, token_cost_per_request}'"
```

Safety guards and guardrail helpers
----------------------------------
- Every script must exit non‑zero on errors and print a one‑line audit: 
  /opt/platform-ops/bin/rw-add-audit.sh "<action>"
- Approval labels: scripts that can change routing (rw-swap-model-variant.sh) require an approval label in the service ticket. If approval header is missing the script refuses to run.
- Rate limiting: prefetch and warmup helpers include a default rate limit (10 requests/s) and token cap (5k) to limit accidental cost spikes.

Add_audit helper (pattern)
--------------------------
Safe, guaranteed append to operator audit log. Example implementation (keeps logs small):

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# /opt/platform-ops/bin/rw-add-audit.sh
set -euo pipefail
MSG="$1"
TS=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
echo "${TS} | ${USER} | ${MSG}" >> /var/log/platform-operator-actions.log || true
# also emit to telemetry-proxy for indexation
curl -s -X POST http://telemetry-proxy.internal/audit -d "{\"ts\": \"${TS}\", \"user\": \"${USER}\", \"msg\": \"${MSG}\"}" || true
```

Operator quick checklist (before running any write action)
---------------------------------------------------------
1. Confirm service and region: rwctl service-info --name inference-prod --region us-east
2. Run the helper in --dry-run and confirm the output.
3. Check token burn projection: sudo /opt/platform-ops/bin/rw-token-burn-estimate.sh --tenant tenant-1234 --minutes 60
4. Add an audit line: sudo /opt/platform-ops/bin/rw-add-audit.sh "planned-action:..."
5. Communicate to #platform-operations and update the incident ticket.

Troubleshooting recipes (fast paths)
-----------------------------------
- If rw-prefetch-model.sh stalls: check telemetry-proxy for rate‑limit responses: curl -s http://telemetry-proxy.internal/ratelimit | jq .
- If rw-swap-model-variant.sh refuses due to missing approval-header: use rwctl ticket-attach --ticket <ID> --label "approved:swap" and retry.
- If rw-drain-tenant.sh reports stuck active requests: identify long‑polls with rwctl request-list --tenant tenant-1234 | grep -E 'tcp|longpoll' and coordinate with the owning product team before force eviction.

Testing checklist for new helpers
--------------------------------
- Unit tests: each script must include a minimal unit test that mocks rwctl and telemetry-proxy.
- Integration test: run nightly in staging with a synthetic tenant and assert no more than 2% added error budget.
- Load safety test: prefetch helpers must pass a burst test that validates token cap and rate limiter.

Rollback and deprecation policy
------------------------------
- If a helper causes unexpected cost or degradation, file an immediate rollback PR to infra/platform-ops and notify the owner team.
- Deprecation: helpers not used for 6 months should be flagged and moved to archived/ with a deprecation notice.

Appendix: Useful rwctl invocations and examples
-----------------------------------------------
# service summary including SLOs and current burn
rwctl service-info --name inference-prod --region us-east --format json | jq '{name, sros: .sros, slo:{p50:.slo.p50, p95:.slo.p95}}'

# list top 10 tenants by token consumption in last hour
curl -s 'http://telemetry-proxy.internal/query?metric=token_usage&window=60m' | jq '.data | sort_by(-.tokens) | .[:10]'
